description: I am a Physiotherapy student passionate about space, science, and astronaut health. I am working on LUNA-SAFE, a project focused on monitoring lunar base safety and astronaut health to detect potential risks. I enjoy research, teamwork, and learning new things. I am looking for creative and motivated team members with skills in coding, AI, data analysis, space science, engineering, or design. Let's make lunar exploration safer!
summary:
LUNA-SAFE is a browser-based simulation prototype designed to support astronaut health monitoring and lunar mission safety.

The project began with an idea to protect future lunar habitats using sensors that could monitor temperature, vibration, structural tilt, and cabin pressure. It then expanded to focus on astronaut health, including heart rate, blood oxygen levels, activity, and health alerts.

As a physiotherapy student, I also introduced a Physical Therapy & Rehabilitation section to support astronaut health before, during, and after space missions. This feature records reported pain, fatigue, exercise activity, and recovery trends.

The prototype demonstrates how astronauts can request medical or rehabilitation reviews and how Mission Control can acknowledge and document those requests. A supporting Site Planner explores lunar terrain using NASA-derived data.

LUNA-SAFE currently uses simulated health readings. Our future goal is to connect a wearable monitoring device and validated sensors to the software, creating a more integrated system for astronaut health and safety.
details:
How LUNA-SAFE Works

LUNA-SAFE is an interactive web application developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It brings astronaut health monitoring, rehabilitation tracking, lunar habitat safety, and site exploration into one interface.

1. Astronaut Health

This section simulates astronaut health readings, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), and activity. It displays alerts when selected values reach demonstration warning thresholds. The health history feature records simulated readings and displays trends over time. Body temperature can also be recorded manually.

2. Medical Assistance and Mission Control

An astronaut can request medical assistance through the application. Mission Control can acknowledge and document the request. The software also demonstrates oxygen-related review requests initiated by an astronaut or Mission Control. These are requests for qualified review, not automatic changes to oxygen delivery or life-support equipment.

3. Physical Therapy & Rehabilitation

This section was inspired by the project developer's physiotherapy background. It includes three mission phases: pre-flight, in-flight, and post-flight.

Users can record discomfort, fatigue, perceived exertion, exercise type, and session duration. The application displays symptom flags, records rehabilitation check-ins, and tracks reported fatigue over time. Users can request a rehabilitation team review, which Mission Control can acknowledge and document.

4. Base Safety

The Base Safety section demonstrates how future sensors could monitor a lunar habitat's temperature, vibration, structural tilt, and pressure conditions. It displays simulated alerts to help explain how environmental monitoring could support crew safety.

5. Site Planner

The Site Planner explores potential lunar habitat locations near Shackleton Rim. The project uses NASA-derived lunar terrain and illumination resources to investigate slope conditions and possible site candidates. These results are exploratory and do not certify any location as safe for construction.

6. Future Wearable Device

A future version could connect a wearable device containing suitable heart rate, oxygen saturation, temperature, and motion sensors. The device would send readings to the software, where they could be recorded, visualized, and reviewed. Hardware accuracy, communication reliability, clinical thresholds, and safety would require further testing and validation.

Technology and Impact

The current prototype runs locally in a web browser and uses simulated health and safety data. Some records can be saved locally and exported as CSV files.

LUNA-SAFE aims to demonstrate how a connected monitoring interface could help astronauts and mission teams recognize changes, document concerns, and coordinate appropriate reviews.

The prototype is not a certified medical device, does not diagnose health conditions, and does not control physical life-support systems.
